intro.TrustedMarkup:
String helpers in Vyrn, over slice and bytes().

Indices and lengths are byte offsets. The case and whitespace helpers are ASCII-only and pass other bytes through, so multi-byte text is never corrupted. Every ?? panic(...) below cuts at an offset the function found by scanning s, at an ASCII byte or at a needle match, so it lies on a character boundary; grep -n "?? panic" lists these claims. substring, padStart and padEnd can receive a bad range and say so.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn fromBytesOr(b: Array<UInt8>, fallback: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: stringFromBytes(b) for bytes known to be valid UTF-8, such as an ASCII transform of valid text. fallback exists only to keep the function total. Decode a fallible byte source with stringFromBytes and handle the Err.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn repeat(s: String, n: Int64) -> String
fn joinWith(parts: Array<String>, sep: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: The elements of parts joined with sep between them.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn substring(s: String, start: Int64, end: Int64) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: A byte-range substring. An out-of-range offset or a cut inside a multi-byte character panics, naming the offset. The one place in std/ that turns a SliceError into a crash; a caller that can receive a bad range calls slice and matches.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn indexOf(s: String, needle: String) -> Option<Int64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The byte offset of the first occurrence of needle in s, or None. An empty needle matches at 0.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn lastIndexOf(s: String, needle: String) -> Option<Int64>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The byte offset of the last occurrence of needle in s, or None. An empty needle matches at s.byteLength.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn split(s: String, sep: String) -> Array<String>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Splits s on every occurrence of sep. Adjacent, leading and trailing separators yield empty segments. An empty sep returns [s] unsplit, because per-byte splitting would cut multi-byte characters.
Splits s into lines on \n, stripping a trailing \r from each, as readLine() does. A trailing newline makes no final empty line.
Splits s on runs of ASCII whitespace, with no empty segments.
s with leading and trailing ASCII whitespace removed.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn replace(s: String, from: String, to: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Every non-overlapping occurrence of from in s replaced with to. An empty from returns s unchanged.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn padStart(s: String, len: Int64, fill: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: s left-padded with fill to at least len bytes. Panics when a multi-byte fill does not tile the padding width.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn padEnd(s: String, len: Int64, fill: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: s right-padded with fill to at least len bytes. Panics when a multi-byte fill does not tile the padding width.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn editDistance(a: String, b: String) -> Int64

prose.TrustedMarkup: The optimal-string-alignment edit distance between a and b, in bytes: insertions, deletions, substitutions and adjacent transpositions, each costing 1.
